mainTopic: When a גוי's kosher-made wine stays permitted: supervision, key and seal, the worry that one גוי covers for another (גומלין), and fear of being caught.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about wine that a Jew made kosher for a גוי. The question is when that wine stays permitted. It depends on where the wine is kept, where a Jew lives, and whether he holds the key or seal. רבי יוחנן corrects the ברייתא: if a Jew lives in the same courtyard, the wine is permitted even without key or seal. The גמרא then works out which case the חכמים are arguing on. It is the case where the Jew lives in a different courtyard: the תנא קמא says key and seal are enough, while the חכמים require real watching. The גמרא also fixes their wording, so the checker must come at unpredictable times. Next, the גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule that 'all domains of גוים are one' is lenient or strict, and a ברייתא shows it is strict, because of cheaters. רבא then rules on two real cases that turn on fear: a sharecropper who fears his powerful master will cover for him, and a גוי who would be caught as a thief will not touch the wine. The amud ends with the closing line of פרק רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Different courtyard: permitted only with key or seal
steps.stepSummary: The end of the earlier ברייתא case: if the Jew lives in a different courtyard, the wine is permitted only when he holds the key or the seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he lives in a different courtyard, the wine is permitted, but only if he holds the key and seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא case that began just before this section. It adds that even when the Jew lives in a different courtyard, the wine is still permitted, but only if he holds the key or seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living in the same courtyard gives enough supervision on its own. Living farther away is weaker, so an extra protection is needed: the Jew must control the key to the room or the seal on the barrels. That way the גוי cannot get at the wine without the Jew knowing.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyard; a shared yard that several houses open onto
Key (to the room where the wine is stored)
Seal (placed on the wine barrels)
Only on condition that

phrases.english: If he lives in another courtyard, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: This finishes a case that started before this section, so 'he' is the Jew from that earlier case.

phrases.english: provided that the key and seal are in his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחָצֵר אַחֶרֶת — מוּתָּר, וְהוּא שֶׁמַּפְתֵּחַ וְחוֹתָם בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא case that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the Jew lives in a different courtyard, the wine is permitted only if he holds the key or the seal.

steps.title: Wine in the non-Jew's domain with a Jew in the same courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A new case: the kosher-made wine is kept in the גוי's own domain. If a Jew lives in that courtyard, the wine is permitted, provided the Jew holds the key and seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone makes a גוי's wine kosher and it is kept in the גוי's domain, and a Jew lives in that same courtyard, it is permitted, but only if the Jew holds the key and seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a harder case: now the wine sits in the גוי's own space. It says the wine is permitted if a Jew lives in the same courtyard and holds the key and seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping the wine in the גוי's domain makes it easier for him to touch it, so this case is stricter than before. Even with a Jew in the same courtyard, this version of the ברייתא still requires key and seal. The next step will challenge exactly this requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes (the wine) kosher, by producing it under Jewish control
His domain, the space he owns or controls
Lives, dwells

phrases.english: One who makes a gentile's wine pure, in his domain,
phrases.notes: 'His domain' here means the גוי's own space, not the Jew's.

phrases.english: and a Jew lives in that same courtyard: it is permitted,
provided that the key and seal are in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier case to a new case where the wine is in the גוי's domain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine in the גוי's domain with a Jew living in the same courtyard is permitted, if the Jew holds key and seal (as first recited).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן corrects the wording: no key or seal needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the reciter to change the text: in the same-courtyard case, the wine is permitted even without key or seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to the reciter: Teach it this way: even if he does not hold the key and seal, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן fixes how the ברייתא was just recited. He says that when a Jew lives in the same courtyard, the key-and-seal condition should be dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the ruling was 'permitted only with key and seal.' Now it becomes 'permitted even without them.' A Jew living in the same courtyard is already enough supervision, because the גוי is afraid of being seen.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the person who memorized and recited ברייתות in the study hall
Even though there is not

steps.confusionAlert: The תנא here is not a sage of the משנה era. He is the study-hall reciter who memorized ברייתות. רבי יוחנן is correcting the wording he recited, not arguing with an ancient authority.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much protection a Jew living nearby gives: in the same courtyard, his presence alone is enough.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְתַנָּא, תָּנֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to the reciter: Teach:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַפְתֵּחַ וְחוֹתָם בְּיָדוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: even if the key and seal are not in his hand, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְתַנָּא, תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the condition recited in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the same-courtyard case, the wine is permitted even without key or seal.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: different courtyard is forbidden even with key and seal
steps.stepSummary: If the Jew lives in a different courtyard while the wine is in the גוי's domain, רבי מאיר forbids it, even if the Jew holds the key and seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he lives in a different courtyard, it is forbidden, even if the key and seal are in his hand. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with the case of wine in the גוי's domain. It says that if the Jew lives in a different courtyard, רבי מאיר forbids the wine even with key and seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case (step 1), a different courtyard plus key and seal was enough. Here the wine is in the גוי's own space, so key and seal from a distance do not help. The location of the wine makes the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 1. There, a different courtyard with key and seal was permitted. Here the wine is in the גוי's domain, and that is why it is forbidden.

phrases.english: If he lives in another courtyard, it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמַּפְתֵּחַ וְחוֹתָם בְּיָדוֹ,
phrases.english: even though the key and seal are in his hand;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחָצֵר אַחֶרֶת — אָסוּר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמַּפְתֵּחַ וְחוֹתָם בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the case of wine in the גוי's domain, now with the Jew in a different courtyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine in the גוי's domain with the Jew in a different courtyard is forbidden even with key and seal, according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The חכמים require a guard or an appointed checker
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים forbid the wine unless a guard sits there watching it, or an appointed person comes to check it at set times.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים forbid it, unless a guard sits and watches, or an appointed person comes at set times.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings the view of the חכמים. They say the wine stays forbidden unless real watching is in place: either a guard sitting there, or an appointed person who comes to check at set times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of looking at key and seal, the חכמים ask about actual watching. They give two ways to meet that standard: a guard who stays with the wine, or an official who checks on it at set times.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view)
A guard who sits and watches
An appointed official
Set times, fixed intervals

steps.whatToRemember: Same courtyard: permitted, even without key or seal (per רבי יוחנן). Different courtyard: רבי מאיר forbids even with key and seal. The חכמים require a sitting guard or an appointed checker. Steps 6-9 work out which case they are actually arguing about, and step 11 corrects the 'set times' wording.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis forbid it,
unless there is a guard sitting and watching,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא מְמוּנֶּה הַבָּא לְקִיצִּין.
phrases.english: or unless an appointed person comes, one who comes at set times.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא שׁוֹמֵר יוֹשֵׁב וּמְשַׁמֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view of the חכמים. Which earlier clause they are arguing on is unclear here; steps 6-9 work it out, and it turns out not to be רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine is forbidden unless a guard sits and watches it, or an appointed person comes to check it at set times.

steps.title: Which clause are the חכמים arguing on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case in the ברייתא the חכמים are responding to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים: which case are they talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next few steps: which clause of the ברייתא are the חכמים arguing against?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has several cases: wine in a courtyard where a Jew lives, and wine where the Jew lives in a different courtyard. The חכמים' strict rule (step 5) must be aimed at one of them. The גמרא will now test each option.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? Which case is meant?
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: The Rabbis: to which case are they referring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which earlier clause the חכמים' ruling in step 5 is responding to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the ברייתא the חכמים are disagreeing with.

steps.title: Not the last clause: the תנא קמא already forbids there
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים cannot be arguing on the last clause, since the first תנא already forbids the wine there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they refer to the last clause, that cannot be, because the first תנא also forbids there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, that the חכמים are arguing on the last clause, and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last clause (step 4), רבי מאיר, the תנא קמא, already forbids the wine even with key and seal. The חכמים also forbid, so there is no argument. A dispute needs two different opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposing an option)
The last clause of a teaching
The first, unnamed opinion in a teaching

phrases.english: If we say they refer to the last clause,

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא נָמֵי מֵיסָר קָא אָסַר!
phrases.english: the first tanna also forbids it!
phrases.notes: The first תנא here is רבי מאיר from step 4, who forbids even with key and seal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects the first possible answer to step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects placing the חכמים' ruling on the last clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no disagreement there, since רבי מאיר already forbids.

steps.title: Not the first part of the last clause: רבי יוחנן permits there
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים cannot be arguing on the same-courtyard case, because רבי יוחנן ruled that it is permitted even without key or seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps they refer to the first part of the last clause? But רבי יוחנן told the reciter to teach that it is permitted even without key and seal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second option, the case where the Jew lives in the same courtyard, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, רבי יוחנן changed the text so that the same-courtyard case is permitted even with no key or seal. If the חכמים forbade it unless there is a guard, רבי יוחנן's ruling would go against the חכמים. The גמרא assumes he would not rule against them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the last clause
But look, isn't it so that (introduces a problem)

phrases.english: Rather, perhaps they refer to the first part of the last clause.
phrases.notes: This is the case from steps 2 and 3: wine in the גוי's domain, with a Jew living in that same courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְתַנָּא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say to the reciter:
Teach: even though
he does not have the key and seal in his hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects the second possible answer to step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects placing the חכמים' ruling on the same-courtyard case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would put רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling against the חכמים.

steps.title: The חכמים argue on the different-courtyard case in the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are arguing on the last part of the first clause, where the Jew lives in another courtyard and the first תנא permits with key and seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they refer to the last part of the first clause. The first תנא says: in a different courtyard it is permitted, as long as he has the key and seal. The חכמים say: it is always forbidden unless a guard sits and watches, or an appointed person comes at set times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the חכמים are arguing on the case from step 1, where the Jew lives in a different courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is a real disagreement. The first תנא says a key and seal are enough. The חכמים say a key and seal are not enough, and the wine needs active watching: a guard sitting there, or an appointed person who comes to check.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the first clause
A different courtyard
Key and seal
An appointed person, a supervisor
At set, fixed times

phrases.english: Rather, they refer to the last part of the first clause,
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 1.

phrases.english: where the first tanna says:
If the Jew lives in another courtyard, it is permitted,
as long as the key and seal are in his hand.
And the Rabbis say: it is always forbidden,
unless a guard is sitting and watching,
or unless an appointed person comes
who comes at set times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting two options, gives the correct placement of the חכמים' ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים argue on the different-courtyard case, where the first תנא permits with key and seal and they require active watching.
steps.whatToRemember: The real dispute: when the Jew lives in a different courtyard, the first תנא says key and seal are enough, while the חכמים require someone actively watching.

steps.title: A watcher on a fixed schedule is a weakness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a supervisor who comes at set times is worse, since the גוי knows when he is safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: An appointed person who comes at set times is a weakness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording 'who comes at set times' in the חכמים' statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the supervisor has a fixed schedule, the גוי knows exactly when he will not show up and can touch the wine then. So a fixed schedule makes the protection weaker, not stronger. That cannot be what the חכמים meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A weakness, something that makes it worse

phrases.english: An appointed person who comes at set times
is a weakness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the חכמים' statement just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'הבא לקיצין' in the חכמים' ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A predictable schedule lets the גוי know when he is unwatched, so it weakens the protection.

steps.title: Fix the wording: a watcher who does not come at set times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the text: the supervisor must come at unpredictable times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it: unless an appointed person comes who does not come at set times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The correct version says the supervisor does not come at set times. Because the גוי never knows when he might appear, he will be afraid to touch the wine at any time.

keyTerms.meaning: Who does not come at set times

phrases.english: Rather, read: unless an appointed person comes
who does not come at set times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא מְמוּנֶּה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא לְקִיצִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection of step 10 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The text said the supervisor comes at set times.
steps.terutzMaskana: The supervisor must come at unpredictable times, so the גוי always fears being caught.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a regular schedule is the stronger kind of watching. Here the גמרא says the opposite: surprise visits are what protect the wine.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: all gentile domains are one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says all domains of גוים count as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: the domain of גוים is all one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement from the משנה, setting up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement is short and unclear: it says different גוי domains are treated as one. It doesn't say whether this makes the law easier or stricter. The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The domain or property of גוים
It is all one, treated the same

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
The domain of gentiles is all one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All גוי domains are treated as one.

steps.title: Lenient or strict?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר meant his rule as a leniency or a stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: does רבי שמעון בן אלעזר come to be lenient or to be strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how to understand רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All one' could cut either way. It could mean every גוי domain is equally unsafe, which is strict. Or it could mean the different domains don't make a difference, which could be lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
To be lenient
To be strict

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Does Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar come
to be lenient or to be strict?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the statement quoted in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule is a leniency or a stringency.

steps.title: Two reports from זעירי: lenient or strict
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of זעירי that it is lenient, and רב נחמן reports in the name of זעירי that it is strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of זעירי: to be lenient. רב נחמן said in the name of זעירי: to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers, and both quote the same teacher, זעירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers to step 13 appear here. רב יהודה and רב נחמן each report זעירי's teaching differently, so the question is answered two ways.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Ze'eiri says: to be lenient.
Rav Naḥman says that Ze'eiri says: to be strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lenient according to רב יהודה's report of זעירי; strict according to רב נחמן's report of זעירי.
steps.confusionAlert: Both answers come from the same teacher, זעירי. The disagreement is over what זעירי said, not between two different teachers.

steps.title: רב יהודה's reading: the תנא קמא forbids even in another gentile's domain
steps.stepSummary: According to רב יהודה in the name of זעירי, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is lenient. So the תנא קמא must be strict: the wine is forbidden in another גוי's domain too, because we worry about collusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of זעירי: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר comes to be lenient. This is what the תנא קמא means: just as the wine is forbidden in the גוי's own domain, it is also forbidden in another גוי's domain. We are worried the two will do favors for each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out רב יהודה's view. If רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the lenient one, then the תנא קמא must be the strict one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling one opinion lenient only makes sense if the other opinion is stricter. So the תנא קמא forbids the wine even when it sits in a different גוי's domain. The reason is גומלין: the second גוי may let the first one touch the wine and keep quiet, and the first will return the favor another time.

keyTerms.meaning: to be lenient
and this is what he is saying (introduces a reading of an opinion)
the first, unnamed Tanna of the משנה
domain, area under someone's control
we are concerned about collusion, people doing favors for each other

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Ze'eiri said: he comes to be lenient,
phrases.notes: "He" here is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The גמרא is now explaining the short report from the last step.

phrases.english: and this is what the first Tanna is saying:
just as in his own domain it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ בִּרְשׁוּת גּוֹי אַחֵר נָמֵי אָסוּר,
phrases.english: so too in the domain of another gentile it is also forbidden,
and we are concerned about collusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר זְעֵירִי לְהָקֵל, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב יהודה's short report from step 14 by showing how it changes the reading of the תנא קמא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is lenient, what does the תנא קמא hold?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא forbids the wine even in another גוי's domain, because of the worry of collusion.

steps.title: רב יהודה's reading: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר permits in another gentile's domain
steps.stepSummary: According to רב יהודה, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר limits the prohibition to the גוי's own domain. In another גוי's domain the wine is permitted, and we do not worry about collusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: when is it forbidden? Only in the גוי's own domain. But in another גוי's domain it is permitted, and we are not worried that they will cover for each other.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב יהודה's picture. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees with the תנא קמא and permits the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר limits the prohibition to the owner's own domain. Wine left in a different גוי's domain is permitted, because we do not suspect the two גוים of covering for each other.

keyTerms.meaning: in what case were these words said? (limits a rule to a specific case)
in his own domain
permitted

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
In what case is this said? In his own domain,
but in the domain of another gentile, it is permitted,
and we are not concerned about collusion.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה: the תנא קמא is strict (another גוי's domain is forbidden), and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is lenient (it is permitted).
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יהודה's reading by giving רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's lenient position.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר permits wine in another גוי's domain and does not worry about collusion.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reading: the תנא קמא permits in another gentile's domain
steps.stepSummary: According to רב נחמן in the name of זעירי, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is strict. So the תנא קמא must be the lenient one: only the גוי's own domain is forbidden, and another גוי's domain is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of זעירי: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר comes to be strict. This is what the תנא קמא means: when is it forbidden? Only in the גוי's own domain. But in another גוי's domain it is permitted, and we are not worried that they will cover for each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the opposite view, רב נחמן's. Here the roles flip, and the תנא קמא is the lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'במה דברים אמורים, ברשותו' are the same ones given to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in רב יהודה's reading. Now they are given to the תנא קמא. So the same lenient ruling just moves to a different speaker.

keyTerms.meaning: to be strict

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. The lenient words are the same in both. Only the person who says them changes: in רב יהודה's reading it is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and in רב נחמן's reading it is the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Ze'eiri said: he comes to be strict,
and this is what the first Tanna is saying:
In what case is this said? In his own domain,
but in the domain of another gentile, it is permitted,
and we are not concerned about collusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר זְעֵירִי לְהַחְמִיר, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading to steps 15-16, now following רב נחמן's report.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is strict, what does the תנא קמא hold?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא forbids the wine only in the גוי's own domain and permits it in another גוי's domain.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reading: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids in all gentile domains
steps.stepSummary: According to רב נחמן, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that all domains of גוים are one. So the wine is forbidden even in another גוי's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: all domains of גוים are one.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב נחמן's picture. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the strict one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'one' means every גוי's domain counts like the owner's own domain. So the wine is forbidden everywhere a גוי is in charge, because we suspect the גוים may cover for each other.

keyTerms.meaning: all
the domain of gentiles
it is one, it counts as a single category

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן: the תנא קמא is lenient (another גוי's domain is permitted), and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is strict (all domains of גוים are one, so it is forbidden).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
All the domain of gentiles is one.
phrases.notes: In this reading, any גוי's domain counts just like the owner's own domain, so the wine is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כֹּל רְשׁוּת גּוֹיִם אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב נחמן's reading by giving רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's strict position.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר treats every גוי's domain as one and forbids the wine.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן: 'because of the tricksters'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר saying all domains of גוים are one 'because of the tricksters.' A worry about tricksters only makes sense as a reason to be strict, so this supports רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that fits רב נחמן's report that זעירי called it strict: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, all domains of גוים are one, because of the tricksters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof for רב נחמן's reading. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's own stated reason shows that he was being strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds the reason 'מפני הרמאין,' because of the tricksters. Worrying about cheaters is a reason to forbid, not to permit. So רבי שמעון בן אלעזר must be the strict one, just as רב נחמן said.

keyTerms.meaning: in line with him, supporting his view
because of
tricksters, swindlers

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא backs רב נחמן: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is strict and treats all domains of גוים as one, because of people who might cheat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles which reading of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר has support from an earlier source. The words 'all domains are one' could have gone either way, but the stated reason shows they are strict.

phrases.english: It was taught in line with Rav Nachman,
who said that Ze'eiri said: to be strict:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
All the domain of gentiles is one
because of the tricksters.
phrases.notes: This added reason is the proof. Worrying about cheaters only makes sense if he is being strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for the reading laid out in steps 17-18.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's report that זעירי understood רבי שמעון בן אלעזר as strict.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives the reason 'מפני הרמאין,' a reason that only fits a strict ruling.

steps.title: The vizier's wine and the רבנן's first thought
steps.stepSummary: Wine from the household of פרזק רופילא was left with his sharecroppers. The רבנן before רבא thought there was no worry of גומלין, because the sharecroppers never store things with the vizier.
steps.simpleTranslation: The household of פרזק the vizier put wine with their sharecroppers. The רבנן in front of רבא wanted to say: we only worry about collusion when two people store things with each other back and forth. Here the sharecropper never stores things in the vizier's house, so we should not worry about collusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case and gives the רבנן's first idea about it. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry of גומלין is that one גוי covers for another because they do favors for each other. The רבנן argue that this only happens when the favors go both ways. Here the sharecropper never stores anything with the vizier, so they see no deal between them and no reason to cover up.

keyTerms.meaning: Parzak the vizier, a powerful official
A sharecropper who works someone else's field for a share of the crop
Collusion; returning favors, so one person covers for the other
The Rabbis thought to say; a first idea that may be rejected

phrases.english: The household of Parzak the vizier
placed wine with their sharecroppers.
The Rabbis before Rava thought to say:
When we worry about collusion,
that applies only where
this one places things with that one,
phrases.notes: He means the two of them store things with each other both ways, so each owes the other.

phrases.english: but here, since his sharecropper

phrases.aramaic: לָאו דַּרְכֵּיהּ לְאוֹתוֹבֵיהּ בֵּי פַּרְזַק רוּפִילָא
phrases.english: is not accustomed to place things in the house of Parzak the vizier,
we do not worry about collusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the worry of גומלין from the earlier argument to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First idea of the רבנן: no worry of גומלין when the favors only go one way.

steps.title: רבא: fear makes the cover-up even more likely
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the רבנן's idea. Even the opinion that does not worry about גומלין only means a case where the other גוי is not afraid. A sharecropper who fears his master will cover for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to them: The opposite is true. Even the one who says we do not worry about collusion only means a case where the one is not afraid of the other. Here the sharecropper is afraid of the vizier, so he will cover up for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the רבנן and says this case is actually worse, not better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן only looked at whether favors go both ways. רבא adds a new reason to cover up: fear. A weak sharecropper who is scared of a powerful vizier will protect him, so the wine is forbidden even according to the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the reverse is true
Is afraid of
Covers up for him

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons one גוי might cover for another: trading favors, and fear. When the other גוי is afraid of the owner, we worry about a cover-up even according to the lenient opinion.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not just say the רבנן are wrong. With 'אדרבה' he points to the same relationship they saw as safe: the sharecropper and the powerful vizier do not trade favors. That relationship is a reason to be strict, because the sharecropper is afraid of the vizier.

phrases.english: Rava said to them: On the contrary,
even according to the one who says
phrases.notes: This points back to the lenient side of the earlier argument about another גוי's domain.

phrases.english: we do not worry about collusion,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא מִירְתַת מִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: that applies only where he is not afraid of him,
but here, since he is afraid of him,
he covers up for him in his favor.
phrases.notes: He would say the vizier never touched the wine, even if he did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבנן's lenient idea from step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that there is no worry of גומלין in the vizier's case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן ignored fear. A sharecropper who fears his master will cover for him even without favors going both ways.

steps.title: A גוי found among a Jew's wine barrels
steps.stepSummary: A גוי was found standing among a Jew's wine barrels. רבא rules: if he would be caught as a thief for touching it, the wine is permitted; if not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain city where a Jew's wine was kept, and a גוי was found standing among the barrels. רבא said: If he would be caught as a thief for it, the wine is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case and gives רבא's ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether we assume the גוי touched the wine. If touching it would get him caught as a thief, he is too scared to handle it, so the wine stays permitted. If nobody would treat him as a thief, we assume he touched it and the wine is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A city or large town
Barrels or jugs of wine
Caught and treated as a thief
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: Like רבא's answer about the vizier, this ruling depends on fear. Here the fear of being caught works the other way and keeps the wine permitted.

phrases.english: There was a certain city
in which a Jew's wine was kept.
A gentile was found
standing among the barrels.
Rava said:
If he would be caught over it as a thief,
the wine is permitted;
and if not, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא כַּרְכָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּיהּ חַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new practical case, also decided by רבא, that turns on the גוי's fear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי found among the barrels: if he would be caught as a thief, the wine is permitted; otherwise it is forbidden.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the פרק רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק. It closes the chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. We say this line to show we hope to come back and learn this פרק again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; said at the end of a chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק רבי ישמעאל is complete.
